# Extend the headless arena to simulate the full shipped campaign (waves, levels, upgrades)

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW

## Headline

The automated-balancing harness's headless arena currently models a single fixed skirmish, so its report's `waveReached`, `levelReached` and `upgradesSelected` fields are always empty — extend it to drive the shared campaign wave/level sequencer and upgrade-choice flow so the full shipped campaign can be balanced from evidence.

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) reports full balance statistics, but two fields in its versioned schema are never populated by a real run because the headless arena does not model campaign progression or upgrade selection:

1. **Limit #1 — wave/level progression is not simulated.** The arena models a *single fixed skirmish*: a seed-derived spawn reservoir of hostiles with no wave sequencer, no `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry events, and no level transitions. Consequently `waveReached` and `levelReached` are **always 0** in a batch report (observed on a live `--batch --games 10` run), so the campaign difficulty curves (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) cannot be tuned with this tool. Today the only influence the difficulty curve has is the number of hostile *reservoir* waves.
2. **Limit #2 — upgrade/power-up choice balance is not simulated.** The arena collects power-ups but never drives the upgrade-choice flow, so `choice_selected` events are absent and `upgradesSelected` is always `(none)` in the report. Per-upgrade balance therefore cannot be measured from bot runs.

The arena is intentionally a simplification (a "closed-loop headless arena, not Phaser"), but the epic's own acceptance criteria claim the report captures "wave/level reached" and "upgrades selected (per upgrade/choice id)". They are present in the schema but empty in practice. To balance **the full campaign shipped in the game**, the harness must exercise the same wave/level sequencer and upgrade-choice flow that the game does — through the shared core, not a divergent copy.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want a bot batch to play the *same campaign the game ships* (all levels/waves, with upgrade choices), so I can tune per-wave difficulty targets and per-upgrade balance from evidence instead of intuition.
- **As the automated-balancing maintainer**, I want the arena to drive the shared wave sequencer and upgrade-choice system, so a change to those systems is measured by the batch.
- **As a producer**, I want the campaign-tuning evidence to come from the shipped campaign definition, so a report reflects what players experience.

## Scope

- Drive the **shared campaign/wave sequencer** (the system that consumes `difficulty-curves.csv` and the hand-authored `LEVELS`) inside the headless arena, emitting the real `wave_start` / `wave_cleared` / `level_cleared` telemetry the analyzer already understands, so `waveReached` and `levelReached` become meaningful distributions.
- Drive the **shared upgrade-choice flow** so the bot makes (or receives) upgrade selections and `choice_selected` events are emitted, populating `upgradesSelected` per choice id.
- Keep every piece of gameplay behaviour coming from the **shared core** (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, the upgrade-choice system) — no divergent copy. This is the gym↔game parity convention: an enabled behaviour must run the same code in a gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Document the fidelity boundary precisely: what is now modelled (campaign progression, upgrade choices) and what remains simplified (VFX, formations, rendering).

## Non-goals

- No production runtime changes.
- No rendering/Phaser dependency in the eval core (`src/ai/eval/` stays pure: no wall clock, no I/O).

## Suggested approach

- Prototype sequencer integration first (spike within the item): confirm the shared wave sequencer and upgrade-choice system can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses.
- Emit the canonical telemetry records rather than inventing new event types so the existing metrics/balance-stats extraction picks them up unchanged (`src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` already defines `wave_start`, `wave_cleared`, `level_cleared`, `choice_selected`; `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` already parses them).
- Extend the batch runner to optionally run a full campaign per seed (with a bounded tick budget), and report per-wave / per-level distributions.
- Reuse the existing determinism guarantees: same seed + config + policy ⇒ byte-identical report, now covering the campaign path.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1: Campaign progression simulated.** A headless run plays through the shared wave/level sequencer using the shipped campaign definition (all levels and waves, including `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes), emitting real `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry. A batch report therefore shows non-zero, meaningful `waveReached` and `levelReached` distributions.
- **AC2: Upgrade choices simulated.** The bot makes upgrade selections through the shared upgrade-choice flow and `choice_selected` events are emitted; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC3: Single source of truth.** The arena consumes the shared wave sequencer / upgrade-choice system directly (asserted by test and the existing duplicate-body/parity guards); no divergent copy of campaign, enemy, ship or upgrade stats exists in `src/ai/eval/`.
- **AC4: Determinism preserved.** Same seed + config + policy ⇒ byte-identical campaign report; `recordsHash` stable; no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core.
- **AC5: Config sensitivity.** Editing `difficulty-curves.csv` (e.g. raising a wave's `targetDifficulty`) and/or an upgrade definition measurably changes the corresponding report distribution for the same seeds, verified by test.
- **AC6: Fidelity boundary documented.** `docs/BALANCING.md` (and/or `docs/EVALUATION.md`) states exactly what campaign behaviour is now modelled and what remains simplified, so consumers do not over-read the report.
- **AC7: Tests.** Campaign progression, upgrade-choice emission, single-source-of-truth, config sensitivity and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **AC8: Bounded resources.** A full-campaign batch over ~100 games still completes in a practical time and bounded memory on a dev machine (incremental aggregation, per-run summaries only).
- **AC9: All related documentation is updated** (code comments, `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, README).
- **AC10: Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Risks, assumptions and mitigations

- **Fidelity risk:** running the real sequencer headless may pull in Phaser-coupled code. *Mitigation:* confirm the shared core's headless-safety during the spike; keep the pure eval layer free of rendering.
- **Scope-creep risk:** this item is about *simulating* the campaign, not retuning it. Actual tuning changes remain separate work items.
- **Parity risk:** a divergent arena copy would violate gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1). *Mitigation:* consume the shared core; rely on the existing equivalence guards.
- **Determinism risk:** campaign RNG (dynamic/curve generation) must derive from the run seed exactly as the game does. *Mitigation:* reuse `createSeededRng` and the game's seed derivation; test byte-identical replay.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the headless arena; needs to drive the shared wave sequencer + upgrade-choice flow
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — telemetry/types consumed by metrics; add config surface for campaign runs
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — already parses `wave_*`/`level_cleared`/`choice_selected`; verify/keep
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` / `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — batch runner + aggregation; extend for full-campaign runs
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — batch CLI flags for the campaign path
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — shared wave sequencer to consume (parity source of truth)
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (LEVELS, fixed/curve/dynamic modes, R1 opening-wave curation)
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — shared config loaders (difficulty curves, enemy/ship configs)
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — canonical event names (`wave_start`, `wave_cleared`, `level_cleared`, `choice_selected`)
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — the campaign difficulty targets the arena will now honour
- `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` — fidelity boundary documentation

## Related work

- **Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — the framework this extends.
- **Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation** (AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ) — the schema/aggregation these campaign fields populate.
- **Automate the balance-tuning loop** (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) — the comparison loop that will consume these richer reports.
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only)** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — shares the schema; becomes directly comparable once campaign stats are populated.
- **Periodically validate the human experience against the intended experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — depends on richer campaign evidence.
- **Integrate enemy classification into wave generation and balance tooling** (AH-0MV29XQ0H009P9WP) — balance-rule consumer.
- Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the work item's seed context (the automated-balancing epic AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW, the observed empty `waveReached`/`levelReached`/`upgradesSelected` on a live `--batch --games 10` run, and the repo's shared sequencer/telemetry structure) already sufficed to draft a complete brief.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW** – Automated Balancing (completed)
- **AH-0MV81YJQP008L9CQ** – Balance statistics schema and pure aggregation (completed)
- **AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715** – Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff (open)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv1dluz8009ocjw, 0mv29xq0h009p9wp, absent, ac1, ac10 (+273 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac10, ac2, ac3 (+255 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, 0mv29xq0h009p9wp, absent, ac1, ac3 (+238 more)
data.title: Extend the headless arena to simulate the full shipped campaign (waves, levels, upgrades)

data.description: Each level should be 10 waves. At the end of each level we have a mini-boss. Each level will have a different set of enemy types. Each progressively more difficult than the last. That is Level 1 is easier than level 2. All previous level enemy types can appear in the higher levels (all level 1 enemies can appear in level 2 etc.). When a mini-boss is destroyed the player gets to upgrade any 1 of their existing permanent weapons/power-ups. There are 10 levels before we get to the final boss. We can save the game at each mini-boss and restart rather than starting a new game when returning. When defeating the mini-boss the player can choose an additional weapon type or upgrade that becomes unlocked (50% of them are locked at level 1). We will need at least 10 new aliens and at least 5 new power-ups and 5 new weapon types for the later levels.
data.title: Increase the number of waves in the levels, add mini-bosses
